item.title: Yankees Reveal Whether Giancarlo Stanton Will Be Back With Team
item.description: New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton Giancarlo Stanton missed most of the New York Yankees' season this year, and there was speculation that the team could finally move on from him this winter. When healthy, Stanton is an impact bat with tons of power. However, he has not been healthy too often. He is 37 years old, and the Yankees owe him $15 million for next season. He has a $15 million club option with a $10 million buyout for 2028. Despite rumors of the Yankees potentially moving on, general manager Brian Cashman made it clear that Stanton is not going anywhere. "There's never been a time when he's healthy that he's not been impactful," Cashman said on Tuesday . "If he's healthy, I know he can impact. I know he can get streaky and all that stuff, but he's an impact hitter, and always has been. Hopefully we'll get a healthy Stanton. He's a big presence in our clubhouse, a great leader. He's wired right. He's doing everything he possibly can to impact us in a real positive way. He's not going anywhere. He'll be in spring training with us, without a doubt." Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Stanton is 44 home runs shy of 500 and has a strong case for the Hall of Fame when he retires. He is strictly going to be a designated hitter, which means the Yankees will have to keep Aaron Judge in the outfield. Judge is a capable defender, but as he gets older, keeping him off his feet should become a priority. The Yankees saw what can happen to their offense when he's hurt, and moving him to a full-time designated hitter role soon should be considered. The Yankees cannot do that with Stanton on the team, so it looks like Judge will be in right field again next year. More MLB: Reds Slugger Wins 2026 NL Rookie Of The Year

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Injured Feyi-Waboso is our Robinson – Sinfield
item.description: Feyi-Waboso had a superb second-minute score ruled out for a forward pass in a previous phase during Sunday's win over Australia [Getty Images] Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, England's prolific but injury-prone wing, is the 2026 team's equivalent of Rugby World Cup winner Jason Robinson says assistant coach Kevin Sinfield. Feyi-Waboso has scored nine tries in 17 appearances for England since making his Test debut against Italy in 2024. However, his progress with England has been checked by a string of injuries. He missed the 2025 Six Nations with a shoulder injury, while his 2026 tournament was ended by a hamstring injury sustained in training before England's opening-round win over Wales. He returned this summer, scoring in wins over Fiji and Argentina, but suffered an autumn-ending ankle injury in the first half of Sunday's match against Australia. Robinson, whose acceleration and side-step brought him 28 tries in 51 appearances for England between 2001 and 2007, tore his hamstring in the Rugby World Cup final defeat by South Africa in his final Test. "He is our Jason Robinson," said Sinfield, who played against Robinson during the pair's days in rugby league. "When you have a player who is that explosive and that powerful sometimes a run of injuries just happens. "He's across everything to do with his body and hopefully we get him back firing as soon as we can. "That collaboration [between England and Feyi-Waboso's club Exeter] is going be really important because these guys play a lot of rugby. "Making sure they're fit for those big games is going to be really important." England have the final say over the fitness and conditioning of centrally-contracted players such as Feyi-Waboso, but there have been disagreements in the past with Exeter over his treatment. Relations have since improved with England signing off Fey-Waboso's return for June's Prem final, only three weeks after he suffered a facial fracture. Feyi-Waboso played on after suffering his ankle injury in the 32nd minute of Sunday's 45-22 win over the Wallabies, hobbling his way to half-time before being replaced. Sinfield said that the desire of Feyi-Waboso, who is studying medicine, to stay on the pitch swayed the decision to keep him on. "It's getting the balance right, because the player is telling you he wants to try and run it off," said Sinfield. "You can't scan anyone on the grass, so you're looking at it with your eyes. I think it's only right for us, as coaches, that we listen to players." England will be without Ollie Chessum, George Furbank and Seb Atkinson for Saturday's match against Japan, while flanker Tom Curry has, like Feyi-Waboso, been ruled out of the entire autumn campaign after he aggravated a long-standing hip issue. item.title: CB Dylan Haley decommits from Tennessee
item.description: Flowery Branch (Ga.) Cherokee Bluff cornerback Dylan Haley , a three-star prospect in the 2027 class, decommitted from Tennessee on Tuesday. He had been committed to the Volunteers since June. Haley originally picked Tennessee over offers from Ole Miss , Georgia Tech , Georgia and Auburn , among others. “After much prayer, thought, and conversations with my family, I have decided to decommit from the University of Tennessee and reopen my recruitment,” Haley posted on social media. “I am grateful for the relationships I’ve built and the opportunities I’ve been given.” The Rivals Industry Rankings , a weighted average that utilizes all three major recruiting services, ranks Haley as the No. 552 prospect in the 2027 class and the No. 57 cornerback nationally. He’s listed at 6-foot-1 and 180 pounds. Tennessee’s 2027 class Tennessee sits at No. 22 nationally and 10th in the SEC in the Rivals Industry Team Rankings . Haley’s exit leaves Josh Heupel ‘s program with 18 commitments in the 2027 class. Five-star running back David Gabriel Georges (No. 8) is the top-ranked pledge in the Vols’ class. Wide receiver Kesean Bowman (No. 69) and linebacker Kenneth Simon II (No. 156) are among the six four-stars pledged to Heupel’s program. Tennessee still has three cornerbacks committed: three-stars Slim Leavell (No. 659), Preston Glasco (No. 720) and Carter Jamison (No. 1,164). Glasco committed Oct. 28.

item.title: Kirk Cousins has 3-word message for Fernando Mendoza after Raiders trade
item.description: Fernandomania has officially begun in the desert. With the Las Vegas Raiders trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings in before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, Las Vegas are expected to turn to Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 pick in the draft earlier this year, under center. Mendoza is slated to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at home on Sunday, Nov. 15 (4:05 ET). Mendoza’s lone regular-season action came during his debut, at the end of a Week 4 road loss to the New England Patriots on Oct. 11. He finished 6-for-8 passing for 48 yards. Mendoza’s first two opponents boast vaunted defensive units. Seattle’s defense, dubbed the “Dark Side” for a reason, did not allow a touchdown last week to the undermanned Arizona Cardinals. Looking ahead, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11. Denver ranks in the top 10 in points allowed per game (20.7), sacks (26) and takeaways (12). "I feel that Fernando has done a great job,” Cousins told reporters Oct. 26. “He has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try and go out there and play as well as I possibly can and try and win and give him a good example to learn from." On his Instagram story, Cousins offered a goodbye to “Raider Nation” and a message to Mendoza, whom Cousins tagged in the post. “Go get em (sic),” Cousins wrote. Toughening matters for Mendoza on the field will be the lack of a rushing attack for the Raiders. First-round talent Ashton Jeanty from the 2025 draft has not worked out, although rookie Mike Washington has shown some juice in the backfield. Still, Las Vegas ranks 31st in rushing yards per game (71.3) and is last in yards per rush (2.9). Similar to Cousins, Mendoza will likely have to shoulder much of the output in the Raiders’ offense. “The game has to be balanced,” head coach Klint Kubiak said following the team’s most recent loss to the San Francisco 49ers that dropped their record to 4-5. “You can’t be a running and throwing team when you're throwing it every time. That's not easy. “You got to start the game a lot faster. You got to go toe-to-toe in the first half so that the second half isn't a throwing fest.” The good news is that tight end Brock Bowers ranks ninth in the league in receiving yards and provides a crucial red-zone target with six touchdowns already this season. Wide receiver Tre Tucker emerged as a reliable downfield option for Cousins, which gives Mendoza more relief in the passing game. item.description: Domeiro Bobb-Semple (right) scored a goal in each half for the Bees youngsters [Getty Images] Brentford U21 and League One side Leicester City both moved into the knockout stages of the Jersey Mike's Trophy with vital victories. The Bees had to beat the Football League's basement side Crawley Town in their final fixture in Southern Group H to progress and did so courtesy of a Domeiro Bobb-Semple double in a 2-1 success at Broadfield Stadium, where Connor Wickham scored on his Crawley debut. In Southern Group B, the Foxes trailed at the King Power Stadium against League Two Walsall, who would have gone through in place of their hosts with a win. But strikes from Will Smallbone and John Lundstram put them ahead by the break and they held on. Stevenage topped the group by beating Fulham U21 on penalties. Chelsea U21 were not in action but went through at the expense of Reading , who needed a big win away against Bristol Rovers to see them overtake the west London side in Southern Group C, but the Royals were beaten on penalties. Nottingham Forest U21 and Notts County both eased through into the last 16 with wins in Northern Group F. Forest enjoyed a 3-0 success against League Two promotion-chasers Grimsby Town at Blundell Park, where all the goals came before the break. The Magpies moved into the knockout stages as group winners by beating League One Burton Albion by the same scoreline for a third win in three EFL Trophy games. In Southern Group F, Leyton Orient needed a big victory over Barnet to claim an unlikely second-placed finish on goal difference, but they were well beaten at The Hive, with Jack Maskell's first-half strike setting the hosts on the way to a 4-2 win. item.title: AFC Team Shows Interest in Ex-Steelers Kicker
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls in a preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Aug. 16, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now A former kicker of the Pittsburgh Steelers could soon have a new home in the NFL. The Miami Dolphins worked out former Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls on Tuesday, according to NFL insider Aaron Wilson of Houston’s KPRC2 . #Dolphins worked out Marcus Banks, Daniel Carlson, Cameron Dorner, Kahlef Hailassie, Chris Hilton, Austin Reed, Ben Sauls, Christopher Smith, Bailey Zappe — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 10, 2026 Sauls, 25, was just released by the New York Giants in September and has been looking for his next opportunity since. Sauls played his collegiate career at the University of Pittsburgh and signed with the Steelers as an undrafted free agent out of the 2025 NFL Draft. He impressed during the preseason, making five of his six field goal attempts and going seven of seven on extra points. “Really happy for Ben Sauls. The work he was able to show us,” head coach Mike Tomlin said. “Good for him.” Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls during a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers on Aug. 21, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now However, Sauls’ future in Pittsburgh was always uncertain since the team already had two-time Pro Bowl kicker Chris Boswell on the roster. The Steelers did try to trade Sauls following his standout preseason performance, but they were unable to find a trade partner and waived him ahead of the cutdown day deadline. On Sept. 23, 2025, the Atlanta Falcons signed Sauls to their practice squad. He was then released on Nov. 4 and the Giants signed him one week later. Sauls’ time with the Steelers was brief, but he was still very appreciative of Pittsburgh’s veterans for showing him the ropes at the next level. “To have guys who have been there and done that for years. I mean, the age gap. I think the second youngest is 30, maybe 31. I just turned 24 a couple of weeks ago. I am a breath of fresh air for these guys. But they’ve been there, they’ve done that,” Sauls said. “They reassure me on the field. And to have them with me this whole way. That’s why we just got a silly picture of us. Because I really appreciate what they’ve done for me. And they really took me in and showed me the ropes.” In 2024, Sauls connected on 21 of 24 field goals and a perfect 44 of 44 on extra points at Pitt. He was selected to the Pro Football Focus All-American team and a Lou Groza Collegiate Place-Kicker Award Semifinalist. Overall, Sauls finished his college career hitting on 52 of 64 field-goal attempts, while averaging 63 yards per kickoff. item.title: Dan Le Batard admits he deserves to be called a snitch after uncovering ‘White House’ story
item.description: Credit: The Dan Le Batard Show, FS1 If anyone wants to accuse Dan Le Batard of snitching on the 1990s Dallas Cowboys for their “White House,” he’s not going to argue it. Former NFL wide receiver and current football analyst Andrew Hawkins was on The Dan Le Batard Show Tuesday morning. Hawkins also regularly contributes to Michael Irvin’s sports podcast for Netflix, The White House , prompting Le Batard to express surprise about the show title. ﻿ “Michael Irvin, I am shocked that he has named his show The White House ,” Le Batard said .”For those of you who don’t know some of this backstory, many years ago, when the Super Bowl was in Miami, I, showing no judgement at all that was good as news judgement, put in the 30th paragraph of a story that the Cowboys had a white house in Dallas that they called the White House to have parties with people who were not their wives.” The White House was known as the NFL’s biggest party house in the ’90s. Some have compared it to a brothel, Irvin has described it as a “safe place for camaraderie.” Details on the house began to leak in 1996 after Irvin was involved in a hotel-room drug and prostitution arrest. But according to Le Batard, he put the Cowboys White House in the 30th paragraph of a story about sex and the Super Bowl decades ago. The admission by Le Batard garnered unison chants of “snitch” from the rest of the show. An accusation Le Batard didn’t even bother to deny. “It’s fair,” Le Batard admitted. “It’s actually fair commentary. But I put it in the 30th paragraph, I just tossed it in at the end.” “No one has ever called me a snitch before on that. And I deserve it. I absolutely deserve it,” Le Batard added. “Pablo Torre is getting some snitch stuff, but that’s not snitch stuff. What we just did there is snitch stuff. But it was the 30th paragraph.” Le Batard may have been one of the first to reference the infamous Cowboys White House in mainstream media, but it was only a matter of time before someone blew the roof off that safe place for camaraderie to expose it. item.description: Scott Brown reveals hilarious disguise he wore to avoid Celtic fans at the darts Celtic legend Scott Brown has revealed he once attended the darts dressed as a Minion to avoid being recognised by supporters. The former Hoops captain made the hilarious admission ahead of taking on former European champion Ross Smith at a darts exhibition event in Edinburgh. Brown, who enjoyed a trophy-laden career at Celtic Park, swapped his football boots for darts and even sported a specially-made shirt featuring his iconic No.8. He said: “I have been to the darts before dressed up as a Minion; nobody ever knew I was there! “I really do enjoy the darts. item.title: Luiten Backs McIlroy’s Plan To Cut PGA Tour Cards
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy wants to slash the number of European players who earn PGA Tour cards, and Joost Luiten agrees with the move. The Dutch veteran told GolfMagic that limiting the spots is actually good for the DP World Tour. Limiting the spots could stop the drain of top talent moving across the Atlantic before their prime. Luiten believes the current system of ten cards is too generous and hurts the European circuit. He told GolfMagic, “It means there will be less cards next year, and I think three or four cards will be a good number so that we don’t lose all of our top players.” McIlroy made similar comments last week at the Abu Dhabi Championship. “I thought five was a nice number,” McIlroy said. “I think it would probably be a little less than that. I’d say it’ll probably be four. If I know what I’m talking about, which I usually do!” The Alliance Clock Is Ticking The strategic alliance between the two tours runs until the end of 2027, forcing a new deal before 2028 changes take hold. Luiten noted the urgency of this timeline in his interview with GolfMagic. “All I know about the alliance is that 2027 is the last year and we need to come to a new agreement for 2028,” Luiten added. “It will be very interesting to see how that deal is going to look.” The current setup lets the top ten in the Race to Dubai earn cards if they do not already hold membership. That path might disappear or shrink significantly under the new structure. McIlroy thinks the PGA Tour was leaning toward three spots while the European Tour wanted five. He predicts they will meet in the middle at four. This reduction means fewer Europeans get a direct shot at the biggest purses in the world. It forces players to stay and fight on home soil rather than taking a lateral move to the Challenger Series. Luiten sees this as a necessary step to keep the tour competitive. Keeping Talent in Europe The fear is that top players will leave if the pathway becomes too hard or too easy. Too many cards mean Europe loses its stars. Too few might kill the dream for rising prospects. Luiten argues that three or four is the sweet spot. It keeps the pressure high but ensures the best remain visible on the DP World Tour. McIlroy’s influence as a six-time major winner gives his weight to this argument. The upcoming DP World Tour Championship in Dubai will test the current standings before the new rules arrive. Eugenio Chacarra leads the Race to Dubai, but McIlroy is close behind. The winner on Sunday earns a crucial 2,000-point bump according to Yahoo Sports . With 1,335 points awarded for second and 752 for third, the payouts are set. How Chacarra performs will determine if McIlroy secures his eighth Race to Dubai title, catching Montgomerie. item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns continue to disagree over Mason McCormick’s takedown of Jared Verse during their November 1 game. The incident drew criticism from Cleveland and prompted a response from Pittsburgh special teams coordinator Danny Crossman. Crossman rejected the Browns’ claims, while Verse expressed frustration over the play and his teammates’ response. Steelers coach defends Mason McCormick over Jared Verse incident Pittsburgh Steelers special teams coordinator Danny Crossman has rejected the Cleveland Browns’ accusation that guard Mason McCormick intentionally hit Jared Verse during a special teams play . The comments followed criticism from Browns special teams coordinator Byron Storer after the teams’ November 1 meeting. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick (66) looks on before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. On Chris Boswell’s extra-point attempt, Verse jumped to block the kick, but McCormick grabbed him in midair and brought him to the ground. Officials penalized McCormick 15 yards for unnecessary roughness. Verse recorded one assisted tackle and no sacks in the game, while McCormick started at guard for the Steelers and played the entire contest. Verse later expressed his frustration with McCormick’s actions, saying , “To do something like that, I just can’t have respect for that.” He was also unhappy with how quickly his teammates responded after McCormick brought him down. Explaining his actions, he said, “I really had no idea who it was. I just felt somebody jump and we’re told to get jumpers’ hands down, and that’s really it.” Storer criticized McCormick’s actions, saying an attempt to stop a kick block did not justify taking an opponent’s legs out and bringing him down. He viewed the play as different from the usual effort to prevent an opponent from blocking a kick. Crossman rejected that interpretation, maintaining that players do not take the field intending to hurt opponents. Although McCormick received a penalty during the game, a November 7 report confirmed that the NFL did not issue a fine. item.description: Jessica Pegula makes a return on her way to victory over Marta Kostyuk at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (Luke Hales) Jessica Pegula reignited her challenge at the season-ending WTA Finals on Tuesday, battling past Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk in straight sets to stay on course for a semi-final berth. Pegula, beaten by Coco Gauff in her opening group game at Indian Wells on Sunday, overcame a topsy-turvy second set to win 6-2, 7-5. The win means Pegula can advance to the last four with a victory over Czech eighth seed Linda Noskova in her final group game. Kostyuk is eliminated following the defeat. "I feel like I'm playing well," Pegula said. "I felt my match against Coco was a super high-level match and that was a great match today. "It's so tricky with her because you just don't know what's gonna come -– she will just step in and inject pace, she'll come and kamikaze the net, she goes for returns or her serve can get hot. That's what makes it difficult to play her." The 32-year-old American had looked in complete control in the first set, breaking Kostyuk in the first and seventh games to take the opener 6-2. A chaotic second set began with four consecutive service breaks before Kostyuk held for a 3-2 lead. The Ukrainian then had a break point in the next game but was unable to take advantage as Pegula held for 3-3. The next four games went with serve but Pegula finally grabbed the decisive break in the 11th game. She converted her fourth break point to take a 6-5 lead before holding for the match, sealing victory when Kostyuk smacked a forehand long. rcw/amz

item.title: Inconsistent offense emerging as biggest Cowboys storyline for Week 10
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys survived a battle with the Indianapolis Colts , scoring the go-ahead touchdown with just over a minute left in the game. The much-maligned defense ended the game on a Caleb Downs interception, holding on for a 27-23 win. The game was closer than it should have been , with the team unable to play complementary football to put their opponent away. Dallas has played well defensively for the first half of the last two contests, but the offense hasn’t capitalized to put the games out of reach. The team's inconsistency has been a major storyline for Dallas throughout the season. The offense plays well, the defense falls apart. The defense starts to find its way, the offense slips, and the special teams have gone from good kickers with bad coverage units to a strength in returns and coverage, but an inconsistent kicking game. Is this a symptom of a poorly coached team, or one with a talent issue? Can Dallas figure out a way to play well and keep it up week after week while improving in other areas, or will they remain up and down every game? The offense is becoming inconsistent and unreliable The defense led the way in the Cowboys’ victory in Indianapolis while the offense filled the stat sheet but was wildly inconsistent. A fumble followed their opening field goal drive. They went on a 15-play, 65-yard touchdown drive that took over seven minutes—then followed that up with a three-and-out and two more drives that ended in punts after four plays. Dallas scored a touchdown before halftime and had a three-and-out on their first drive of the third quarter. Later, they went on a 10-play field-goal drive and followed it with a fumble. That has been the Dallas offense for most of the 2026 season. They accumulated over 500 yards against the Colts. Threw for 329 yards and added 179 rushing, but also converted less than 33% of their third-down plays. They owned time of possession with over 35 minutes, but lost two fumbles. Inconsistency kept the Colts in this contest , and that has to change with the upcoming schedule Dallas has. Quinnen Williams is playing like an All Pro Whether it was adapting to a new defense, getting used to his teammates, or dealing with an injury, Quinnen Williams took a few games to reach the level Dallas expected when they traded a first- and second-round pick for him, but he is officially there now. Due to a poor overall defense, Williams might not get the recognition he deserves, but he is playing like an All-Pro. He started a three-game sack streak with his sack against the Green Bay Packers. He added two tackles for a loss, a pass deflection, and two QB hits in that game. The next week, against the Philadelphia Eagles, he had a sack, three tackles for a loss, and a QB hit. The Arizona Cardinals game was his first multi-sack contest, with two, adding seven tackles, and two QB hits. The sack streak ended against the Colts, but he had another seven tackles, three tackles for a loss, and added his second forced fumble

item.title: NWSL legend Jess Fishlock calls it a career after 24 years in emotional farewell
item.description: NWSL and Wales legend Jess Fishlock made her final professional appearance on Sunday -Credit:Dustin Satloff, NWSL via Getty Images Wales icon Jess Fishlock has brought the curtain down on her remarkable playing career after 24 extraordinary years. The 39-year-old played her final match for Seattle Reign over the weekend, a 1-0 loss to Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off quarter-finals. The midfielder was visibly moved as she walked off the field after being substituted on in the 74th minute, with her teammates equally struggling to contain their emotions when she delivered a farewell speech following the game. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT’s Antonee Robinson claims Mauricio Pochettino ‘focused’ despite Manchester United links Jess Fishlock's team-mates were in tears as she said goodbye "No tears. I've had a great career," she told them via Wales Online . "I've loved it." Fishlock will now join Rhian Wilkinson's coaching staff for the upcoming FIFA Women's World Cup play-off against Norway in December, having previously retired from international football in October 2025. She did so having netted 48 goals in 166 appearances, both of which stand as records for any player in either the men's or women's game. Fishlock began her career with Cardiff City back in 2002 and went on to compete in eight different countries. She also collected UEFA Women's Champions League winners' medals with FFC Frankfurt and Olympique Lyonnais. Having additionally won three NWSL Shields throughout a 14-season tenure with Seattle, she announced back in April that this season would mark her last. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "I've loved it," an emotional Fishlock told the BBC , as she wiped away tears after losing to Gotham on Sunday. "And the truth is I've loved that my last year was with this group, because they have just given me so much, and not just on the field. "I look back and there's just so much to think about, not only with Reign but with Wales," she added. "It would have to be one of those panorama snapshots because it's too difficult. "All I know is what I'm most proud of deeply in my soul is that... I've stayed with Wales - that was difficult for 20 years, wouldn't do it any other way - stayed with the Reign for 14 years, wouldn't do it any other way. "Because for me, when you win with your people - with the people that you've struggled with, the people that you've lost with, the people that you've failed with - when you win with your people, there is no better feeling in the world."

item.title: Ravens Part Ways Former Steelers Tight End
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Nick Vannett at practice on Sep. 26, 2019 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now A former tight end of the Pittsburgh Steelers is looking for a new home in the NFL. The Baltimore Ravens released former Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Nick Vannett on Tuesday, the team announced . We have released TE Nick Vannett and guard Kyle Hergel. We have also released guard Michael Jordan from the practice squad and signed FB Lucas Scott to the practice squad. — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) November 10, 2026 Vannett, 33, joined the Ravens in September after he was released by the Seattle Seahawks as part of their final roster cuts. He joined the Steelers via a trade midway through the 2019 season. The team sent a fifth-round pick in the 2020 NFL Draft to Seattle in exchange for Vannett. However, Vannett did not have much of an impact in Pittsburgh, recording just 13 catches for 128 yards and zero touchdowns in 13 games. Buffalo Bills cornerback Tre’Davious White tackles Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Nick Vannett on Dec. 15, 2019. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Vannett began his NFL career as a third-round pick in the 2016 NFL Draft out of Ohio State, where he had 91 catches for 877 yards and six touchdowns over five seasons. He spent the first three years of his career with the Seahawks before being dealt to the Steelers. During that span, he racked up 48 catches for 463 yards and four touchdowns. Following his one-year stint in Pittsburgh, Vannett joined the Denver Broncos for the 2020 season. He continued to disappoint in Denver, though, recording just 14 catches for 95 yards and one touchdown in 15 games. Vannett then signed with the New Orleans Saints in 2021 and for half of the 2022 season until he was released on Nov. 19. He joined the New York Giants shortly after and finished the season with the G-Men. He then spent the 2023 season with the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers, but he caught just one pass for three yards in eight games (five starts) with the Chargers. Vannett bounced back in 2024 with the Tennessee Titans, catching 17 passes for 135 yards and three touchdowns, tying his career-best mark. He then signed with the Vikings ahead of the 2025 season but failed to record a statistic and was eventually signed off Minnesota’s pratice squad by the Los Angeles Rams, where he finished the season. A native of Westerville, Ohio, Vannett has recorded 108 receptions for 1,012 yards and nine touchdowns in his professional career.
